parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Find work with friction
parts.body:
Start discovery at a workflow, not a model demo. Follow one unit of work from its trigger to its outcome. Record the volume and variation of cases, time spent waiting and doing work, handoffs, rework, and the information people need at each decision. Listen to the staff who handle exceptions; an executive process chart often omits the cases that consume the most judgment. Observe a sample across teams, channels, and regions before extrapolating.

Separate a bottleneck from a symptom. A claims officer may spend 20 minutes reading documents because the case file is disorganized, while the real delay is a week waiting for missing information. Summarization may improve the officer's task without moving total resolution time. Draw a simple value stream with touch time and elapsed time. Name where quality fails and who bears the cost. Include customers or workers who may be affected by an error.

List interventions along a range: change a rule or handoff, improve search, assist a person with drafting or extraction, automate a bounded step, or redesign the process. Estimate potential value only after testing which constraint each intervention changes. NIST's Map function calls for documenting intended purpose, context, affected people, and business value; this keeps use-case discovery anchored to the actual work.

example.title: The wrong bottleneck
example.body: A team spends 18 minutes drafting a response but waits four days for a missing document. A drafting copilot could free capacity; it will not by itself meet a two-day resolution target. The figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Map ten cases
exercise.body: Follow ten recent work items through a process. Record elapsed and touch time at each step, exceptions, rework, decision owner, and affected person. Circle the largest delay and write two interventions, including one that uses no AI.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map context and purpose

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Design a narrow first experiment
parts.body:
A use case is more testable when its boundary is precise. For a claims team, 'AI handles claims' conceals many separate tasks: intake classification, document extraction, policy lookup, loss estimation, fraud review, decision, and explanation. Choose one step with a named user and an observable output. A source-linked document summary for an adjuster is narrower than an automated coverage decision. It still needs evidence that the cited text is correct and access to only the case material the adjuster may see.

Write the intended use, excluded uses, population, data sources, human actions, output destination, and failure path. Define the smallest representative evaluation set, including common and difficult cases. Have practitioners judge whether an output saves time after correction and whether omissions could harm a customer. If the output informs a consequential decision, the human reviewer must have enough source context and time to challenge it; a nominal approval button gives little protection.

Regional scope can change the experiment. EU use involving personal data must satisfy applicable GDPR principles; some AI uses may also fall into AI Act high-risk categories depending on intended purpose. Canada has federal and provincial privacy regimes whose application depends on the organization and activity. Ask legal and privacy owners to classify the actual use. Do not generalize an employment or credit rule to every claims summary.

example.title: A bounded claims test
example.body: Twenty adjusters receive cited summaries of repair estimates for a limited class of property claims. They decide coverage as before and mark missing or inaccurate facts. The pilot excludes automatic denial and does not allow the assistant to send a customer message.

exercise.title: Write a use-case card
exercise.body: State the trigger, user, source data, permitted output, excluded decision, human review, likely error, and test cases for one proposed use. Explain which law or policy classification the privacy and legal teams must confirm before the pilot.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map and Measure
EU AI Act Service Desk: Annex III

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Estimate value and test feasibility
parts.body:
Build a rough value model using case volume, current labor or loss per case, the portion the intervention can affect, expected adoption, and the time or quality change after human correction. Subtract integration, training, supervision, model calls, monitoring, and ongoing content maintenance. A 30% reduction in drafting time on 10% of cases has a much smaller effect on the whole operation than a headline demonstration suggests. State whether released time becomes capacity, faster service, or a cash saving.

Feasibility has more than one axis. A use case may have strong model performance on clean samples but poor access to current policies, no reliable labels, or a workforce unable to review outputs within the service window. Test source quality and permissions before funding a polished prototype. Define the errors you can tolerate, their severity, and the fallback when a source is absent. Sample by region and case type so average performance does not hide a weak subgroup.

Set a discovery gate. Continue only if the source data can be used, evaluation cases represent the work, the business sponsor commits to workflow change, and the plausible benefit still exceeds the full operating cost. Fund another small experiment if one uncertainty is decisive and cheap to resolve. Stop when the bottleneck belongs elsewhere. NIST advises measuring performance in deployment context and managing risks using the resulting evidence.

example.title: A transparent capacity estimate
example.body: A team processes 40,000 cases yearly. Drafting takes 15 minutes on 60% of them; an assistant might save five minutes after review. The gross potential is 2,000 hours before adoption, implementation, supervision, and error correction. These hypothetical inputs should be replaced by observed case data.

exercise.title: Calculate and challenge value
exercise.body: Use a real or hypothetical workflow to calculate gross annual hours or avoided loss. Apply a conservative adoption rate and subtract review and operating costs. List the two assumptions that would most change the result and propose a low-cost test for each.

sources: NIST AI RMF Playbook: Measure in context
NIST AI RMF Playbook: Manage tradeoffs

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Turn discovery into a decision
parts.body:
A discovery backlog should contain evidence, not just idea names. Give every candidate a problem statement, owner, affected population, workflow boundary, baseline, plausible intervention, data and control dependencies, estimated value range, confidence level, and next decision. Group closely related ideas that share a data or platform dependency, but keep their benefit cases separate. An enterprise search platform may serve several teams; each workflow still needs its own evaluation.

Bring candidates to a review with an explicit recommendation: test, defer, redesign, or stop. Explain what new information the test will buy and who will act on it. If the team cannot tell whether a prototype worked, the next budget should fund measurement design. If a workflow has many irreversible customer consequences, start with decision support or a shadow evaluation before delegating an action. Involve the people doing the work in reviewing cases and the proposed fallback.

Avoid letting available data alone choose the portfolio. A convenient dataset can make a low-value experiment look easy. Equally, a valuable problem with weak data may warrant a staged cleanup rather than immediate rejection. Document the dependency and compare its cost with the expected benefit. This gives the CAIO a defensible way to discuss difficult bets with business, finance, and control leaders.

example.title: Three recommendations
example.body: Test a cited summary for adjusters because source files are accessible and review is already part of the workflow. Defer a cross-region policy adviser until conflicting versions are reconciled. Stop an automatic denial proposal until its legal classification, appeal path, and error tolerance are understood.

exercise.title: Hold a discovery review
exercise.body: Prepare three use-case cards and assign test, defer, redesign, or stop to each. For the test candidate, specify the maximum spend, evaluation sample, responsible business owner, control reviews, and decision date.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map, Measure, Manage
